A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework and experiments, with main text and appendices available for comparison. The clipped final table in v2 can be recovered from its embedded text and matched to v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of five LLaMA/Gemma models, consumer-credit experiments, human validation, and temperature sensitivity results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds distributional case studies and robustness estimates in Appendices C and G.

M1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds direct decomposition of whole-vector dispersion using trace covariance, extending v2's coordinate/projection-based treatment of embeddings. The scalar and categorical decompositions, ICI formula, and implemented prompt-generation pipeline remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Coverage remains quantitative guesstimation across five domains, plus loan approval and credit-risk rating. The new case studies stay within this coverage, while robustness checks vary analysis settings. Reasoning models, tool use, and adversarial paraphrases are proposed future evaluations.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain the same three LLaMA and two Gemma models. Section 4.1 corrects 'LLaMA 27B' to 'Gemma 27B', matching the already-correct Figure 4; this does not introduce a comparator. Alternative likelihood specifications are robustness variants of the estimator.

E3.justification: New Appendix G introduces balanced subsampling without replacement at 5, 10, 15, 20, and 25 responses per cell, plus alternative response-family fits. Appendix C adds KDE-based distribution comparisons. Previously reported main-experiment and temperature-sweep settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands supplementary validation with tests of response-count sensitivity and Gaussian versus heavy-tailed assumptions in Tables 3–4. Figures 7–9 additionally examine overlapping intent distributions, separated intents, and articulation-driven shifts through concrete cases. The earlier temperature analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix G broadens statistical estimation through Laplace and Student-t specifications alongside Gaussian fitting. Existing 100-replicate bootstrap procedures and 95% confidence-interval reporting are unchanged. The added robustness tables do not report uncertainty intervals or an increase in independent runs.

E6.justification: Existing result plots and human-validation tables are unchanged. New results include IS ranging from 0.382 to 0.387 across response counts in Table 3, likelihood-sensitivity estimates in Table 4, and case-specific values such as Gemma 27B AS = 0.693 in Figure 9. These are supplementary findings, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 introduces epsilon-sufficient intent comprehension in Definition 2.6 and derives AS <= epsilon^2/2 under an expectation-dominating distributional distance in Appendix A. It also generalizes the evaluator's value space and supplies an explicit vector-valued variance decomposition in Appendix B.1, substantially extending the formal treatment.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a formal intent-comprehension framework, variance-based diagnostics, and evaluation across models and domains. The abstract and introduction retain the finding that larger evaluated models generally show greater intent sensitivity, with uneven and modest gains.

C2.justification: v3 adds qualifications about residual semantic drift, limited model/domain generalizability, and inability to identify model-family effects directly. It clarifies why high MVS alone does not imply better comprehension and why deterministic decoding need not eliminate underlying aleatoric uncertainty. These refine the retained interpretations.

D1.justification: The new analyses document subsampling without replacement, Student-t degrees of freedom of 5, and how response distributions are pooled for KDE comparisons. Existing generation prompts, filters, extraction procedures, API information, and estimation software remain unchanged; no new code or data access information is provided.

R1.justification: v3 adds connections to speech-act theory, pragmatic generation, semantic uncertainty, and structure-conditional decoding, explicitly positioning its definition as a text-only specialization of Giulianelli (2022). Qin et al. (2021) is removed. Most appendix positioning is retained; the joint-intent survey's author correction concerns the same titled work.

P1.justification: Selected introductory, ICI, free-form-response, and discussion passages are rewritten or expanded, and residual-uncertainty terminology is emphasized. Publication and affiliation text also change. The main section sequence and extensive prompt appendices remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds three KDE figures and two robustness tables, adjusts captions and equation formatting, and relocates retained displays. The final paraphrase table moves from an overflowing column in v2 Appendix K to a readable full-width page in v3 Appendix N. Existing plotted results are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the framework's justification through the approximate definition, estimator robustness checks, and clearer qualifications about interpretation and applicability. The distributional examples aid understanding, and the final table's clipping is repaired. These are useful incremental gains; the main empirical findings remain unchanged, and the new robustness summaries provide limited fitting detail and no accompanying uncertainty intervals.
